joey_coverage.audit_summary: Strong Arbutus, Lyonia, Pyrola and other Ericaceae media, including bark, fruit, twig and unusual mycoheterotrophic form.
joey_coverage.assessment: More than sufficient for the two-taxon local lesson.

family_lesson.where_to_look_first: On the local woody taxa, start with alternate/spiral exstipulate leaves and a fused urn-, bell- or tube-shaped corolla. Then inspect the stamens: poricidal anthers and anther appendages are high-value Ericaceae characters. Finally check ovary position and fruit because these vary across the family.
authoritative_framework: Leaves are commonly spiral/alternate and stipules are absent.
Corolla is usually fused and often urceolate or tubular.
Stamens are commonly 5–10; anthers often have appendages and dehisce through apical pores.
Ovary position varies from superior to inferior across the family.
Fruit may be capsule, berry or drupe, often with a persistent calyx.
avoid_overgeneralizing: Do not require evergreen leathery leaves.
Do not require an urn-shaped flower in every Ericaceae.
Do not assume one ovary position across the family.
Do not assume all Ericaceae fruits are berries.
Do not identify from bark or fruit alone.

teach: contrast with Arbutus habit and bark

confusable_families.Rosaceae: Rosaceae commonly has free petals and many stamens plus hypanthium/fruit architectures unlike the fused Ericaceae corolla with poricidal-anther pattern.
confusable_families.Ebenaceae: Can share woody habit, fused corolla and berry-like fruit; Ericaceae poricidal anthers and typical flower/stamen architecture are stronger tie-breakers.
